Hi Laura — thanks for the questionnaire and sorry for the short delay. Please find high-level answers below and attached reference docs (Redwood_Data_Handling_Brief.pdf and SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf). I've copied Irene from our security team for the deeper operational details.

Short answers (summary for the matrix):
- Data residency: Hosted API customers can select primary region at account setup (us-west, us-east, eu-west, ap-southeast). Request/response payloads are routed and stored in the chosen primary region; metadata and aggregated telemetry used for platform analytics are pseudonymized and stored in multi-region services.
- Retention: Request/response payloads retained for 30 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring; logs (ingestion/request metadata) retained for 90 days; automated backups/snapshots have a 90-day retention policy unless contractually extended.
- Deletion workflow: Customer-initiated account erasure triggers immediate application-layer deletion of tenant records within 24 hours. Backup/snapshot removal is processed as part of scheduled snapshot lifecycle; full expiry and unrecoverable deletion completed within 30 days of request (see details below).
- Regional pinning: Yes — we support tenant-level region pinning for hosted accounts; data never moves outside pinned regions unless the customer authorizes replication or manual export.

Attachments included: Redwood_Data_Handling_Brief.pdf (dataflow diagrams + TTL tables), SOC2-Summary-2025.pdf (attestation excerpt).

If Pacifica needs a one-page attestation or an executable statement for your procurement pack, we can prepare a signed attestation and route via DocuSign. Would you like that?

Best,

Hi Laura,

Appreciate the follow-ups — I work on data controls and ops so wanted to provide the detailed operational responses you requested. Summary answers below; I included links to our internal deletion runbook and snapshot lifecycle playbook for evidence flow.

1) Application-layer deletion vs caches:
- Immediate behavior: When an account erasure is requested, we mark the tenant as "erased" and trigger synchronous removal of persistent tenant records (primary DB, object stores). Ephemeral caches (in-memory worker caches, short-lived KV cache) are cleared synchronously for new requests; however, distributed asynchronous caches (edge caches, long-lived KV replicas) may require a short propagation window. Practically, any in-memory or process-local caches are cleared within the 24-hour application deletion SLA.

2) Backups & snapshots:
- Snapshot lifecycle: Automated full snapshots are kept for 90 days by default. Snapshots are incremental; we maintain a manifest that maps snapshot deltas to tenant objects. On a customer erasure request we mark related snapshot entries as "expunge_pending" and schedule the deletion job.
- Expunge SLA: For hosted accounts, we provide two operational paths: (a) Standard expunge — snapshot entries are processed through our normal lifecycle and removed at natural expiry (within 30 days of request); (b) Accelerated expunge (available on request / via procurement addendum) — we run expedited snapshot deletion and verify removal within 7 business days. Accelerated expunge requires acceptance of a no-recovery window and may have an associated one-time fee.
- Evidence trail: Every snapshot expunge run emits a signed audit record containing snapshot id, tenant id, initiating user (system account id), job id, and completion timestamp. Those records are stored in our immutable audit store (retention 7 years) and can be exported as CSV or provided via a secure link for compliance review.

3) Audit exports for deletion steps:
- Yes — we can generate a deletion audit package that includes: deletion request id, stepwise timestamps, job ids, actor ids (system/service account), and cryptographic hash of the expunge job output. That package can be delivered as a downloadable archive and retained by Pacifica.

Operational notes / links (for your ops team):
- Deletion runbook (read-only): https://drive.google.com/redwood/purge-runbook-2026
- Snapshot lifecycle manifest spec: https://drive.google.com/redwood/snapshot-manifest-spec
- Data handling brief (attached previously): Redwood_Data_Handling_Brief.pdf

If you'd like, Marissa (our Trust lead) and I can join a 30-minute technical call to walk through a sample deletion audit package.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Data Controls
Redwood Inference
